title: Implement frontend UI platform shutdown control and user notification system
description: Add a protected administrative shutdown control in the UI with multi-factor or double-confirmation modal. Display a graceful maintenance/shutdown banner and countdown timer to connected users, disable new transactional submissions, and trigger the backend graceful shutdown workflow while rendering real-time drain and shutdown status.

title: Implement graceful backend shutdown and traffic draining across microservices
description: Configure Spring Boot graceful shutdown (server.shutdown=graceful, spring.lifecycle.timeout-per-shutdown-phase) across all platform services and gateway. Enable and secure the Spring Boot Actuator /actuator/shutdown endpoint. Implement lifecycle hooks to drain active in-flight requests, flush message buffers, release database connection pools gracefully, and deregister from service discovery / gateway before process exit.

title: Move DB credentials out of git into environment variables or local properties
description: Stop storing DB credentials in git. Move username/password out of src/main/resources/application.properties into env vars or a gitignored application-local.properties. The file currently has a live MySQL password.

title: Phase 3: Domain decomposition & database-per-service for automation-service
description: Extract AutomationEntity, AutomationRepository, and ProductAutomationController into services/automation-service. Decouple persistence to a dedicated automation_db schema. Replace raw SQL AdminController with declarative schema migrations (Flyway/Liquibase). Migrate blocking JPA off WebFlux or adopt Spring Data R2DBC.

title: Phase 2: Extract dedicated Spring Cloud Gateway service
description: Scaffold services/api-gateway with Spring Cloud Gateway WebFlux. Move GatewayConfig out of hub, eliminate loopback conflicts, configure dynamic routing (/products/automation/** to automation-service), rate limiting, and circuit breakers with Resilience4j.

title: Phase 1: Refactor repository into a multi-module Gradle layout
description: Decompose the single hub project into a root Gradle multi-module layout (services/api-gateway, services/automation-service, shared/common-dto, etc.). Configure shared dependencies, Gradle toolchain (Java 21), and common build conventions.

title: Migrate Spring API Hub to a True Microservices Platform
description: Transition the monolithic hub application into a decoupled microservices architecture with standalone API gateway, domain-specific services, event-driven async execution, and observability.

title: Offload blocking JPA operations from Netty event loop to boundedElastic scheduler
description: Keep JPA off the Netty event loop. Hub is WebFlux; AutomationRepository.save and friends are blocking. Wrap DB work in Mono.fromCallable(...).subscribeOn(Schedulers.boundedElastic()) (you already do a similar CompletableFuture pattern in JenkinsController.getJenkinsConfigMono).
close_reason: Offloaded blocking JPA operations and system metric calls to Schedulers.boundedElastic() via Mono.fromCallable(), added reactive methods in AutomationService, and updated JenkinsController

title: Fix Gateway route loopback on /products/** fighting internal controllers
description: Don’t treat Gateway as a gateway yet. GatewayConfig sends /products/** back to localhost:8082. Either remove that route or point it at a real downstream service. As written it can fight your own controllers.
close_reason: Removed /products/** loopback route from GatewayConfig so Gateway does not fight internal controllers

title: Fix /admin SQL injection vulnerability by sanitizing tableName
description: Fix /admin SQL. AdminController concatenates tableName into CREATE/SELECT/DROP. That’s easy to break and unsafe. Reuse the sanitizing idea already in AdminService, or drop this UI until you need it.
close_reason: Sanitized tableName across create, query, and drop actions in AdminController using AdminService validation and added unit tests

title: Local Orchestration: Multi-container Docker Compose stack
description: Update compose.yaml to orchestrate the full local microservices platform: MySQL/Postgres databases per service, message broker (Kafka/RabbitMQ), api-gateway, automation-service, and observability containers.

title: Phase 5: Platform observability, service discovery, and centralized config
description: Implement platform-wide production capabilities: Spring Cloud Config / Vault for externalized secrets, Service Discovery (Consul/Eureka/K8s DNS), and distributed tracing with Micrometer Tracing + OpenTelemetry/Zipkin/Prometheus across Gateway and microservices.

title: Phase 4: Decouple host process execution via event-driven runner worker
description: Decouple JenkinsExecutorService host ProcessBuilder/Docker calls. Publish action events (e.g. JenkinsActionRequestedEvent) over Kafka/RabbitMQ consumed by a standalone runner-agent/worker daemon. Stream progress and status back via SSE/WebSockets.

title: Clean up unused stub types (SecurityService, adminUsers, AutomationStateListener, JenkinsLoggingService)
description: Delete or implement empty types so they don’t look like features: SecurityService, adminUsers, AutomationStateListener, JenkinsLoggingService (also not a @Service, so it wouldn’t inject anyway).
close_reason: Deleted unused stub types: SecurityService, adminUsers, AutomationStateListener, JenkinsLoggingService

title: Persist Jenkins process state based on actual compose/PID status
description: Persist process state honestly. JenkinsExecutorService sets status to Running/Stopped without checking compose/PID. Use AutomationActions.isPidRunning / compose status, or the UI will lie after a failed docker compose.
close_reason: Persisted Jenkins process status honestly using isComposeRunning and isPidRunning checks and added unit tests

title: Wire Jenkins config updates (URL, port, credentials) through AutomationService
description: Finish Jenkins config updates. updateFields.js can POST several fields; Jenkins.unpackJenkinsMap only rediscovers on productBasePath. Wire URL/port/user/password/API key through AutomationService.updateAutomationEntity.
close_reason: Wired productURL, productPort, productUserName, productPassword, and productAPIKey updates through AutomationService.updateAutomationEntity and added unit tests

title: Split product pages into shared layout and Jenkins-specific fragments
description: Split product pages. ProductUMLController and ProductMainframeController return pages.html, which is Jenkins-shaped (SSE fields, docker buttons). Use a small shared layout + a Jenkins-only fragment, or those pages will keep lying.
close_reason: Extracted shared layout and created dedicated Jenkins fragment in templates, ensuring non-Jenkins product pages render clean product views

title: Implement GET /products/automation to list AutomationEntity rows
description:
Give ProductAutomationController a real GET. It’s mapped to /products/automation with every method commented out. List AutomationEntity via AutomationService / AutomationRepository. That’s the Entity → Repository → Service → Controller spine in README.md.

Note: Smallest useful first commit: env-based datasource + a working GET /products/automation that lists rows. That unblocks everything else without touching docker or gateway.
close_reason: Implemented GET /products/automation endpoint returning Flux<AutomationEntity> and added unit test

title: Add integration tests with Testcontainers and WebTestClient
description: Add one test that isn’t contextLoads: e.g. AutomationRepository.findByProductName with Testcontainers MySQL, or a WebTestClient GET for / and /products/automation/jenkins.
close_reason: Implemented MySQL Compose service, updated current-stack README, and added passing Testcontainers MySQL + WebTestClient HTTP integration tests; Gradle tests/build and Compose config validated

title: Rewrite README.md to reflect current tech stack and architecture
description: Rewrite README.md to Gradle, Boot 4.1, WebFlux, and “Jenkins product hub,” not Maven + Boot 3.6 REST CRUD. Don’t start the README wishlist (JWT, Redis, Kafka, ClickHouse, ELK, Jaeger) until CRUD + Jenkins start/stop are true.
close_reason: Implemented MySQL Compose service, updated current-stack README, and added passing Testcontainers MySQL + WebTestClient HTTP integration tests; Gradle tests/build and Compose config validated

title: Configure MySQL service in compose.yaml
description: Put MySQL in compose.yaml (or turn Boot docker-compose support back on in build.gradle). HELP.md is right: compose is empty.
close_reason: Implemented MySQL Compose service, updated current-stack README, and added passing Testcontainers MySQL + WebTestClient HTTP integration tests; Gradle tests/build and Compose config validated
